skill.name: container-orchestration
skill.description: Provides Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS/Fargate patterns for containerized application deployment.
skill.summary: Plan and draft container deployment patterns for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS/Fargate.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, local health checks, and safe container hardening patterns. Confirmed issues are unsafe example credential patterns in Compose and Kubernetes templates, a debug listener example bound to all interfaces, and an overly broad Kubernetes RBAC example for secrets.

remediation.issue: Example manifests include concrete credentials and default passwords.
remediation.suggestion: Replace user:pass, supersecretkey, and default Postgres password examples with placeholders and clear instructions to use secret managers or local-only overrides.

remediation.issue: Kubernetes RBAC example grants list access to secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secrets from the generic Role or narrow access to only required named secrets with the minimum verbs needed.

remediation.issue: Debug container example listens on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Mark the debugpy example as local-only and bind it to a safer interface or require explicit port-forwarding guidance.

remediation.issue: Image build script can push to a registry when requested.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must verify registry, tag, and authentication context before running the script with push enabled.

semantic_findings.title: Overly Broad Secret Read Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The Kubernetes RBAC example grants a service account get and list access to secrets. Listing secrets is broader than most applications need and can increase blast radius if the workload is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The manifest explicitly grants verbs get and list on secrets in a production example. This is a clear least-privilege issue, although it may be intended as a generic template.

content.value_statement: Container deployment choices can be difficult to compare and configure safely. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured examples for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS/Fargate workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts production-style Dockerfile examples with multi-stage builds and non-root users.
Provides Docker Compose templates for app, database, cache, and optional worker services.
Shows Kubernetes manifests for deployments, services, ingress, autoscaling, RBAC, and network policy.
Explains Helm chart structure, values files, helper templates, and common Helm commands.
Summarizes AWS ECS/Fargate architecture choices, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, and deployment tooling.
limitations: Does not inspect a live cluster or cloud account without separate tool access.
Examples require adaptation before production use, especially secrets and access control.
Does not replace vendor documentation for version-specific platform behavior.
Included scripts can build and push images only when run in a configured Docker environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a container baseline
use_cases.description: Create an initial Dockerfile and Compose setup for a service before deeper production hardening.

use_cases.title: Compare orchestration options
use_cases.description: Review when Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, or ECS/Fargate fits a deployment need.

use_cases.title: Draft deployment references
use_cases.description: Use the reference manifests as a checklist for probes, resources, security contexts, and rollout settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the container orchestration skill to draft a Dockerfile for my Python web service. Explain each production safety choice in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Add local services
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Docker Compose patterns to create a local stack for an app, Postgres, and Redis. Keep secrets configurable through environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Design Kubernetes manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Kubernetes patterns to draft deployment, service, ingress, HPA, PDB, and network policy guidance for this service.

prompt_templates.title: Choose ECS or Kubernetes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECS on Fargate and Kubernetes for this workload. Include networking, IAM, scaling, deployment, and operations tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Help me containerize a small API service.
output_examples.output: A concise deployment plan with a multi-stage Dockerfile approach, non-root runtime user, health checks, and environment-based configuration guidance.

output_examples.input: I need Kubernetes production patterns for a web app.
output: Deployment guidance with probes and resource limits.
Service and ingress notes for routing.
Autoscaling, disruption budget, and network policy considerations.

output_examples.input: Should I use ECS Fargate or Kubernetes?
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary that compares operations burden, AWS integration, portability, IAM, networking, scaling, and deployment tooling.

best_practices: Replace all placeholder credentials and example hosts before using generated templates.
Verify platform-specific settings against current Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, or AWS documentation.
Review generated manifests for least privilege, network exposure, and secret handling before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example secrets or default passwords into production manifests.
Do not apply generated Kubernetes resources without reviewing RBAC, network policy, and namespaces.
Do not run image build or push scripts against shared registries without confirming the target.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy containers for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and scripts that require user review and execution.

faq.question: Can it help with Docker and Kubernetes together?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Dockerfile, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS/Fargate reference material.

faq.question: Are the included manifests production ready?
faq.answer: They are production-style examples, but they need environment-specific review before use.

faq.question: Does it include cloud-specific guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes AWS ECS on Fargate guidance for networking, IAM, secrets, scaling, and deployments.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude Code, Claude, and Codex as supported tools.

faq.question: What should I review most carefully?
faq.answer: Review secrets, default credentials, RBAC permissions, network exposure, and any image push commands.
